definition: Deep Voodoo is an artificial intelligence-based visual effects studio created by Matt Stone and Trey Parker in 2020.
details: The studio utilizes deepfake technology to create hyperrealistic effects for entertainment purposes.

explainer.lead: Deep Voodoo is a visual-effects studio founded by Matt Stone and Trey Parker in 2020. It uses deepfake technology to create hyperrealistic effects for entertainment, showing how AI can become part of a production studio’s creative toolkit.

tiers.eli5: It is a special-effects studio that uses AI to make actors or faces look convincingly different on screen.
tiers.practitioner: Studios use deepfake models to build hyperrealistic effects for film and TV. The pitfall is treating such output as plug-and-play; convincing results require careful production work around the model.
tiers.paperLevel: A production studio applying deepfake technology, i.e. learned face and video synthesis, to create hyperrealistic effects for entertainment; no formal model specification is given.

explainer.mission: To apply artificial intelligence, particularly deepfake technology, to hyperrealistic visual effects for entertainment.
explainer.founded: Matt Stone and Trey Parker created Deep Voodoo in 2020.
